groups.deck: Doctor Who - The Thirteenth Doctor and Yasmin Khan

zoneSelectionProgress.definition: Observed components and repeated history vectors overlap; they are not unique operations, choices or returns. Retained counts and movements are separate. Complete receipts can have unresolved identities. Missing components/attempts remain unknown and trainingReady remains false.

definitions.records: Parent decisions, standalone STARTED choices, nested target records and search operations; overlapping observations, not unique gameplay decisions. Terminals are not counted again. Includes incomplete, censored and post-outcome records; no learning eligibility claim.
definitions.contextStatuses: One status per observed record; ABSENT means no inputContext. CAPTURED refers only to its named partial profile.
definitions.inputBoundaries: Current version-1 audited boundary inventory for parent/standalone owners, not proof that a legacy producer captured it or every branch selected an option. A missing group means no observed record, not no choices.
definitions.components: Declarations per present context, including unsupported stack/history/options. Missing contexts supply no component declarations.
definitions.omissionReasons: Records carrying each explicit reason; one record can have multiple reasons. Component/reason pairs are also deduplicated within a record.
definitions.optionBindings: Supported profiles have diagnostic options only; no model-facing selectable-option bindings are established. This does not describe diagnostic joins or target provenance.
definitions.knownUnrecordedCaptures: Explicit parent target/search capture-omission counts, separate from observed-record denominators. Missing declarations mean unknown, not zero. Actual missing selector boundaries/times are unknown; attribution is to the parent container only.
definitions.byTurn: Parent baseline or choice-start turn where available; nested/search records use their parent container, not an independently captured selector time. Null turn means unknown. Present entry components supply their own clock with ENTRY_LOCATION; unavailable entries stay null with ENTRY_LOCATION_UNAVAILABLE. playerId remains the owning chooser, not the turn player.

limitations: Main-phase play selection plus observed subordinate callbacks. No complete mulligan, combat, reactive-priority or legal-choice coverage.
Candidate assessments are partial and may repeat an ability; counts are assessment observations, not unique rejected legal actions.
Rejection reasons mix strategic preferences, timing and affordability; they do not establish rules illegality.
Player observations are partial. Missing state includes remembered reveals, detailed mana restrictions and delayed effects.
Win/loss labels describe eventual game outcomes, not whether individual choices were correct. trainingReady remains false.
Search summaries omit per-candidate values and the heuristic counterfactual; actual choice-change rates cannot be inferred.
Action execution joins are available when declared by new records; legacy executions remain UNAVAILABLE. Execution success does not establish resolution or strategic value.

Linked engine events retain resolution, counter, removal, bulk-clear and land-play observations where recorded. Missing events do not establish failure or resolution; downstream effects are not attributed.

Finalized target snapshots describe committed stack targets, not alternatives or why they were selected. They omit identities beyond IDs, later retargeting, and choices made during resolution; legacy or unavailable snapshots are not empty target lists.

Payment snapshots contain recorded engine facts, not every cost decision. lastLifePayment is not a total and must not be summed with phyrexianLifePaid. LKI/current card lists can refer to the same paid card. Counter-removal choices and complete restriction/payment alternatives remain outside this coverage.
Legacy land records and some direct combo selections can lack assessment rows.
UNKNOWN engine/pilot metadata in legacy inputs is retained explicitly rather than guessed.
Handler labels are preserved from Forge: MissingPhaseRestrictions means a phase check declined the play, not necessarily missing card configuration.

Standalone choices cover instrumented target, mode, numeric/X and payment boundaries, including execution and resolution callbacks. Unknown parents, copied modes, missing option pools and capped prefixes remain explicit; alternatives are observed inputs, not complete legal plans.

Completed payment visitors are proposals, not proof of payment. Mana routine outcomes describe that routine only; finalized engine payment facts remain separate. Type text, counter tables and conversion matrices are marked unrecorded. Mana pool choices without an active ability context are not recorded.

Inline input contexts cover audited boundaries only. CAPTURED means the named partial profile was captured, not complete Magic knowledge or every AI input. ABSENT means unavailable capability, not an empty view. Only inputContext.policy is the permitted feature projection; diagnostic joins, original option membership/order, manifests, outcomes and legacy observation fields are excluded. Only directly proved public disclosure associations can be linked; other associations remain unresolved. Stack coverage is profile-declared and bounded where supported; long-term historical knowledge remains incomplete. trainingReady remains false.

V4 retains typed request fields and adds diagnostic current-option links. Those links do not authorize entity pool membership, count or ordering as model features. Direct public disclosure links require delivery proof without an intervening engine event. No profile certifies complete learning examples.

V5 additionally permits exact received scalar mode bounds at audited planning selector/operation entries. These are invocation arguments, not committed rules constraints or mode identities, membership/order, effect semantics, cached-plan cause or a complete legal mode domain. V5 itself grants no other hypothetical prompt permission.

V6 additionally permits exact received total entity bounds and the supplied related-player role at the audited outer entity operation. This operation overlaps its inner selectors. V6 parent links alone grant no history; V7 declares its own history permission below. Entity pool membership/count/order remain excluded. These received arguments may describe planning work and do not certify legal results or complete learning examples.

V7 additionally permits bounded successful-return history within an audited base-controller entity operation at the next selector entry. Current public associations require exact receipt identity/incarnation and fresh local bindings; unresolved identities stay null. Incomplete histories are unavailable, and direct/unaudited selector history remains unknown. No current offered-pool membership/count/order, complete game history or learning readiness follows from this permission.

V8 additionally permits the received single zone-change request at its audited selector: destination, ordered origins, local optionality and current decider role. These invocation arguments do not predict actual movement, authorize offered cards or establish outer repetition/history, effect semantics or learning readiness. None and empty origins retain their request meanings.

V9 additionally permits the received ordinary engine zone-operation iteration request, ordered zones and current source/decider roles at its own entry before reveal. The terminal describes retained cards before later processing, not callback returns or movement. Child links remain diagnostic and grant no zone-selection history. Outer/inner observations overlap; no legal domain, complete history or learning readiness follows.

V10 additionally permits audited ordinary zone-selector progress and bounded prior non-null callback returns at the child entry. Attempts, engine loop positions, non-null returns, retained cards and movement have separate meanings. Current public associations require exact receipt identity/incarnation and fresh local bindings; private/stale identities stay null. Incomplete progress/history is unavailable; direct or unsupported history remains unknown. No offered-pool permission, complete legal domain or learning readiness follows.

V11 identifies audited ordinary, named-list and per-type zone operation branches. Named iteration requests count evaluated named entries, including skipped entries; each type is a separate operation whose retained collection can include earlier types. Branch-local return history is not across-type history. Names, predicates and offered pools receive no additional permission. V11 alone does not cover Heist/Draft; all examples remain incomplete.

V12 additionally permits audited Heist and Draft operation/progress requests. Receipts precede between-pick movement; rejected non-null Heist returns still count without retention. Actual per-call origin-list identities are witnessed independently of the outer descriptor, with bounded ordered value equivalence. Generated, private, moved or stale identities gain no pool/name permission; incomplete history and learning readiness remain unchanged.

V13 records audited effect spell-ability operations and selectors at their own entries and permits only the received outer requestedSelections. The original do-while may return one choice for zero/negative requests; the argument is not a legal result bound. Ability references, option indices and parent links are diagnostic. V13 alone grants no single prompt; V14 describes its narrow request permission below. V14 alone grants no spell-choice history; V15 declares controller-local progress below. Titles, offered pools and complete legal domains remain unknown. All examples remain incomplete.

V14 permits the received single spell-ability affected-Player role for audited null/canonical-empty maps or one-key native HashMaps. Current local bindings require exact Player identity; foreign/unrepresented roles are unavailable. Other maps, keys, null/non-Player Affected values and arbitrary parameters remain unsupported, never silently empty. Diagnostic receipts are not features; no option/domain/history or learning readiness follows.

V15 additionally permits controller-owned spell-choice progress and a bounded prior-return occurrence vector at the next selector. Ability identities stay unresolved (null); detached receipts and IDs remain diagnostic. Only an exact admitted base-controller operation can own this history; direct selectors and external engine repetition remain unknown. Incomplete history is unavailable. No offered-pool, ability-definition, complete domain or learning readiness follows.

V16 independently permits bounded received scalar/current-public-role parameters at audited numeric-range and single-entity callbacks. Unknown maps/keys/values remain unsupported, and unproved/private/stale roles are unavailable. Parameters do not grant offered-pool membership, complete counter/effect/cost semantics or additional numeric planning-domain permission. Role collections remain unsupported; all examples remain incomplete.

V18 permits whole received Attachments/Attackers role lists of at most 64 current public cards at the audited entity callback, including membership/count/order/duplicates. These are request roles, not an offered selectable pool or proof that the current heuristic used them. Unknown/oversized/unresolved requests stay unavailable; trainingReady remains false.

V19 captures typed floating-mana tie requests and their own selector inputs. testPayment=true records planning work, including inside a real parent; non-test calls still inherit their actual rules/planning basis. Legacy list-only requests remain unknown. The offered tie set is diagnostic, not all legal payment plans; selection does not establish spending or successful payment, and trainingReady remains false.

V20 captures the non-test payment-loop mana-source selector before its filtering/reservation work, with the current shard, remaining mana value and received check/effect flags. Offered source abilities remain a diagnostic prefix, and a selected source is a proposal that can be rejected or fail later; no activation/payment or source binding is inferred. trainingReady remains false.

V21 records received discard/sacrifice policy kind and native min/max before existing outer work. These are request values, not a legal card domain or proof of paying a cost; alias/forced/batch paths keep their original behavior. Exile stays post-ranking and inner picks/history remain separate increments. trainingReady remains false.

V22 captures native sacrifice iterations with current remaining diagnostic pools and a whole bounded prior-proposal list from the original local accumulator. Prior cards require exact current-public proof; membership/count/order permission does not extend to the offered pool. Selected cards remain proposals, not paid sacrifices; oversized/unknown/unresolved history stays unavailable and trainingReady remains false.

V23 captures native discard policy/combo/special batch operations at their own entries, including the post-narrowing policy input. Only policy/combo receive a diagnostic pool; special helpers gather their hands internally. Bounds are scope values, null fallthrough is operation-specific, and forced aliases are not invented atomic picks. V23 alone grants no private-history/domain permission; V24 declares its own history grant below. trainingReady remains false.

V24 captures native discard preference probes and fallback iterations with effective counts and bounded prior-proposal history. Only this kind grants exact, unambiguous current chooser-owned visible-hand associations alongside public associations; identical permitted hand presentations refuse history instead of exposing hidden ordering. Preference decline is fallthrough, and fallback entries precede their original sorting and mutations. Offered pools remain diagnostic, payment is not proved and trainingReady remains false.

V25 captures exile ranking at its own entry before original filtering/sorting. Requested count and effect are received scalars; the incoming pool is diagnostic and craft/card semantics remain partial. The legacy PAYMENT_EXILE_POOL subList observation retains its lack of an own entry/view. Results remain proposals, and trainingReady remains false.

V26 captures maximum-X calculation after native free-choice/cache guards and before probes/provisional X changes. The effect flag is a received scalar, not payment or a legal domain. Guarded/cached returns create no calculation. The retained MAX_X_HEURISTIC assignment remains post-computation without an own entry/view; records overlap and trainingReady remains false.

V27 captures the native Draw amount/target helper before its calculations and target reset, including fixed draws. Mandatory is a received helper flag. Boolean results do not prove overall playability, legal targets or payment; numeric refinements retain their original application records without an own entry/view. Observations overlap and trainingReady remains false.

V28 captures Damage play/trigger assessment and life-drain helper entries before their native calculations/target changes, including fixed-damage assessment. Operation and nullable mandatory are received scope fields. Native rating/reason or boolean returns are not overall playability, legal-domain or payment proofs; old refinement application records keep no own entry/view. Observations overlap and trainingReady remains false.

V17 captures the existing trigger-preparation operation before its work and permits only its received mandatory directive. Acceptance/final targets remain results, and nested selectors retain their own actors/entries. Unknown legacy helper directives stay unavailable. This grants no trigger semantics, option domain or learning readiness; legacy absent operation inputs remain unknown.

Invocation accounting covers configured original-AI standalone callback wrappers only. Entries are not unique gameplay decisions. Input-unavailable records are retained records; callback errors are not capture loss. Publication return does not prove collector delivery. Cutoff-pending work is not evidence that a late callback never ran. Parent/nested and uninstrumented invocation counts remain unknown. Partial scopes, legacy absence and overflow cannot supply exact missing-start fractions.

Nested target accounting counts capture-method calls within retained parents, not original selector callback outcomes or game-wide nested decisions. Missing whole-parent events remain unknown. Pending capture calls describe each parent cutoff, not workers necessarily still running at run finish. Legacy parent absence and saturation suppress the aggregate retained-parent missing-row fraction.

Search accounting counts recording-parent capture attempts before host eligibility, not original search callback outcomes or game-wide decisions. Result-stage interruption/failure on retained rows is separate from capture-method omissions. Missing whole parents remain unknown; mixed legacy data and saturation suppress the aggregate retained-parent missing-row fraction.
